comparator.name: Middle Eastern Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Leiden study product identifies the Modern Middle East Studies route and its first-year Arabic language option. The listed unique components support 60 EC in year one, 60 EC in year two and 55 EC in year three, including a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC of genuine open electives. The live product places the same History of Central Asia & Afghanistan module (5852VCAAY, 5 EC) in both the Year 2 compulsory group and the Year 3 route-specific slot. The earlier decision counted it twice to reach 180 EC, although a student cannot earn the same 5 EC twice. The 2026–27 OER confirms the route and degree outcomes but does not resolve which distinct module fills the remaining third-year 5 EC. An archived 2025–26 guide listed a restricted third-year choice that excluded already completed courses, but those options cannot be imported without current-year confirmation. The unsupported duplicate is omitted; this is a 175-EC supported subset, not a complete 180-EC pathway.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is generic Middle Eastern Studies. Of the five current official routes, Modern Middle East Studies has the broadest region-wide historical, cultural, religious, political and economic identity rather than centring one language/culture. It is selected on that academic basis before UCR availability is considered. Arabic is then selected from the route’s four first-year language packages by official listing order.

exception.reason: The current 2026–27 study product assigns the same 5-EC module, History of Central Asia & Afghanistan (5852VCAAY), to both a second-year compulsory position and a third-year route-specific position. Counting it twice would falsely satisfy the 180-EC requirement. The current sources available for this review do not establish a distinct eligible 5-EC third-year replacement. A valid complete comparator pathway cannot be certified until Leiden clarifies that slot.
exception.curriculumContext: The selected broad Modern Middle East Studies route and Arabic first-year language option remain supported. Unique listed components total 175 EC: 60 EC first year, 60 EC second year including History of Central Asia & Afghanistan once, and 55 EC third year including 30 EC open choice and a 10-EC thesis. The apparent third-year duplicate is not counted. The independent UCR review found no sustained Middle Eastern regional and language curriculum, but the no-defensible-match terminal outcome requires a complete 180-EC external reconstruction; revisit it after the 5-EC slot is resolved.
